correctness.rationale: For an edge-open packing, orient every induced star; let \(X\) denote line leaves and \(Y\) point leaves. Each selected edge has one leaf, so \(|B|=|X|+|Y|\). The two leaf types are mutually nonincident. If both occur, fix a line \(L\) in \(X\) and point \(y\) in \(Y\). Let \(Z\) be the off-\(L\) points on other \(X\)-lines. Each such line has \(q\) off-\(L\) points; each point of \(Z\) lies on at most \(q\) such lines since its joining line to \(y\) is forbidden. Hence \(q(|X|-1)\le q|Z|\) and \(|Y|\le q^2-|Z|\), giving \(|B|\le q^2+1<q(q+1)\). If one leaf type occurs, two distinct centers have a joining line that cannot be a leaf; at most \(v-1\) leaves remain. Equality forces this to be the sole missing line, all centers onto it, and every other line to attach to its intersection point. Duality gives the other type and exactly \(2v\) distinct optimal sets. Single-center cases have at most \(q+1\) edges. The argument covers every existing plane of order \(q\ge3\), including non-Desarguesian planes.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary article proves general edge-open-packing bounds and values for several standard families but does not state this point-line incidence classification. Theorem 4.1 of arXiv:2403.00750 characterizes attainment of the generic degree upper bound \(|E|/\delta=v\), not all maximizers at the strictly smaller value \(v-1\). Bounds on the injective chromatic index concern minimum numbers of color classes, not the exact set of largest classes. Actual searches across direct and equivalent formulations and related published work found no theorem implying the full all-order geometric classification and its enumeration. Historical unindexed overlap remains possible.
residual_risks: Earlier equivalence may be described as maximum induced star forest or maximal injective color class in an unindexed combinatorial-geometry source.
The full 1996 technical report by Kelmans was not inspected; its accessible abstract states a different vertex-coverage objective.
Non-Desarguesian finite planes were not computationally sampled; theorem proof depends only on their defining axioms, not on coordinates.
No independent priority review or mathematical audit has been performed.

evidence: RESULT.md: mixed-leaf double count and complete equality classification.
General upper bound and equality case in arXiv:2403.00750v1 establish the structural gap being closed.
limitations: Potential historical overlap under alternative terminology remains as noted under originality.
value.rationale: A canonical infinite class of finite incidence geometries has an exact edge-open-packing invariant, uniform across all existing projective-plane orders \(q\ge3\), without requiring Desarguesian coordinates. The theorem gives a one-step improvement over the generic regular-degree bound together with a complete geometric rigidity and counting classification, not just a scalar special-case value. The mixed-leaf obstruction uses a substantive incidence double count and excludes all other optimal shapes.
